clue.text: Drink of beer knocked back by a prince from India

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but here the word for the drink is turned round end to end

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: An Indian prince downs a glass of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking the beer down, but here it signals a turnaround of the beer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Raja is the traditional title of a Hindu king or prince in India.

clue.text: Give an account of Tralee in novel form

indicators.note: novel here means new or fresh, so the letters of Tralee take a new form

explanation.surface: Someone writes up the Irish town of Tralee as a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' pretends to be a book; it means new, signalling that TRALEE is rearranged. Tralee is a town in County Kerry, Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount or tell a story is to give an account of events, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Crosswords for those with good memories

definitions.text: Crosswords for those with good memories

parts.words: Crosswords for those with good memories
parts.note: jumbo puzzles are extra-large crosswords, and Jumbo is a pet name for an elephant, the creature famed for never forgetting

explanation.surface: A recommendation of crosswords suited to people with sharp recall.
explanation.walkthrough: Elephants are proverbially said never to forget, and large elephants are nicknamed after the famous circus elephant Jumbo; jumbo crosswords are the big weekend puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Supersized puzzles carry this name, and so do elephants, the animals proverbially blessed with long memories.

clue.text: Son quiet after confusing subject

indicators.note: to confuse is to jumble up, so the letters of the two preceding words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A son falls silent after a bewildering topic comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject under discussion is the matter or issue in hand, as in 'the matter in question'.

clue.text: Place to study one half of Manchester's football team

indicators.note: taking one half of the team name keeps only its first three letters of six

parts.note: Manchester United is the famous football club

explanation.surface: Half of Manchester United's squad apparently goes to college.
explanation.walkthrough: Manchester United is one of England's best-known football clubs; its first half leaves the British short word for university.
explanation.definitionFit: Uni is the informal British word for university, an institution where people study.

clue.text: Drug dealer: chap who drives extremely quickly

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
a merchant is a trader or dealer

explanation.surface: A drug pusher is also a man who drives far too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug dealer' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase describes a fast motorist, someone fond of racing along at reckless velocity.

clue.text: I name body put in the picture

parts.note: form means a body or bodily shape

explanation.surface: Someone names a body that has been painted into a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone in the picture is an idiom for telling them the facts, which is to notify them.

clue.text: Family member's new record cut

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A relative's new album has been edited down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling's son is a relation, so the specific kinship term fits the general description.

clue.text: Second American I joined in queue for large car

indicators.note: in tells us the joined pieces are placed within the word for a queue

parts.note: a queue is a line of people
a mo is a moment, a second
US means American

explanation.surface: An American joins a queue for a big car, just for a second.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeured luxury saloon with a long body is the classic example of a large car.

clue.text: Last of many men het up possibly about tabloid's leader

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the newspaper's first letter
possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way
a leader comes at the front, so we take the opening letter of the word tabloid

explanation.surface: Many men get angry, for the last time, about the editorial of a tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MEN HET UP, and 'about' wraps that around T, the first letter given by 'leader'. A newspaper leader is also an editorial, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteenth is an informal ordinal for the latest in a seemingly endless series, as in 'for the nth time'.

clue.text: Back of page showing dandy

indicators.note: back here means the little word is turned backwards rather than meaning the rear of a sheet

explanation.surface: The reverse side of a page displays a well-dressed man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back of page' looks like the last letter of page; instead 'Back' applies only to the little word 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fop is a man overly vain about his clothes and appearance, a synonym for a dandy.

clue.text: A unit of soldiers or travelling actors, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for travelling actors is said aloud and a word of identical sound is written

parts.note: a troupe is a touring company of performers

explanation.surface: A question of whether the group is military or a theatrical company on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: In the army a cavalry or armoured subunit is called by this name, and loosely any group of soldiers.

clue.text: Back Cockney's filly following tip

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the dropped-H horse comes after the word for tip

parts.note: the end is the tip of something

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop the initial H, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a filly is a young female horse

explanation.surface: A tipster backs a Cockney's filly after getting a racing tip.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, the working-class Londoners, famously drop the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a candidate or plan is to support it publicly, a synonym for giving approval.

clue.text: Cream from the East with few calories

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East
lite is the marketing spelling for low-calorie food

explanation.surface: A low-calorie cream imported from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' pretends to be dairy; it means the best of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of society is its select best, the top tier, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Resident's study linked to current sort of Buddhism

parts.note: a den is a private study room
I is the symbol for electric current
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A local's study is linked to a form of Buddhist practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A denizen is an inhabitant of a place, a somewhat literary synonym.

clue.text: Put up with year becoming awkward

parts.note: to stick something is to tolerate it

explanation.surface: Tolerating a whole year of something is turning tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky situation is a difficult or tricky one, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Small bible and a collection of books for learned person

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A scholar's reading list: a small bible and a set of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a scholar of profound knowledge, someone very erudite.

clue.text: Attempting to be tiresome

definitions.meaning: having a go at something, making an effort
annoying or exasperating, as of a difficult person

explanation.surface: Making an effort turns out to be wearisome.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both making an attempt and being exhausting to deal with.

clue.text: An alto unusually discordant

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An alto singer is uncharacteristically out of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Music without a key centre sounds harsh and dissonant to many ears, hence jarring or discordant.

clue.text: Aim to prepare for match

definitions.meaning: to point a weapon or camera at a target
to get fit and practise ahead of a sporting contest

explanation.surface: An athlete's goal is getting ready for the big game.
explanation.definitionFit: One trains a gun on a target, and an athlete trains for a contest.

clue.text: Passage right inside bar

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece is put within the other

parts.note: bar means except, as in 'all bar one'

explanation.surface: A corridor to the right leads inside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means except, as in 'all bar one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage from a book is a quoted extract or section of text.

clue.text: Dance with short man again and again

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man

indicators.note: again and again means the shortened word appears a second and a third time

parts.note: the same words quoted again: a man shortened by his last letter

explanation.surface: Someone dances repeatedly with a man of small stature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts CHAP to CHA, and 'again and again' repeats it twice more.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a lively Latin American ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise that's almost hip these days

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: cool is the current slang for hip or fashionable

explanation.surface: A gasp of astonishment at something nearly trendy nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: Coo is a British interjection expressing astonishment, like 'gosh' or 'blimey'.

clue.text: Small hotel or pub: money-spinner to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only a portion of the clue word is used

explanation.surface: A small hotel or pub that brings in good money.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub, often one offering rooms, so it is both a small hotel and a tavern.

clue.text: But one could be a Himalayan creature

parts.note: yet means but, as a conjunction
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hesitant suggestion that something might be a mountain beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of legend is said to roam the high mountains of Nepal and Tibet.

clue.text: Left posh lass somewhere in Europe

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
U means upper-class, posh
a gal is a girl, a lass

explanation.surface: An upper-class girl has departed for a European destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like departed but is the nautical word for the left-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: Portugal is a country on the Iberian peninsula, so it is an example of a place in Europe.
